# Kyoto Spring Trip Plan: 5 Days, 2 Adults

A relaxed Kyoto itinerary built around temples, easy walks, local food, and one low-transit day trip. Costs are estimated in **JPY** for **2 adults**, excluding flights, and aim to stay within your **USD 1,800** total budget.

# Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Cost Estimate

## Day 1 — Higashiyama Welcome Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive in Kyoto, check in, and keep the first half-day light with a gentle walk around **Maruyama Park** and **Yasaka Shrine**.
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Kodaiji** or **Chion-in** for a quieter temple start, then wander the preserved lanes of **Ninenzaka/Sannenzaka** early before peak crowds.
- **Food:** Try a simple Kyoto set meal with yuba, tofu, or soba near Gion.
- **Estimated cost:** **JPY 18,000–24,000**
  - Lodging: 12,000–16,000
  - Food: 5,000–6,500
  - Local transit / entries: 1,000–1,500
- **Best night base:** **Gion / Higashiyama** for walkability and low-transit access to temples

## Day 2 — Arashiyama at an Early Pace
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Start early at **Tenryu-ji** and the **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** before the busiest hours.
- **Afternoon:** Cross **Togetsukyo Bridge**, then choose one slower stop such as **Okochi Sanso Garden** or a riverside tea break instead of stacking too many sights.
- **Food:** Lunch on **tofu cuisine** or a seasonal soba meal in Arashiyama.
- **Estimated cost:** **JPY 19,000–26,000**
  - Lodging: 12,000–16,000
  - Food: 5,500–7,000
  - Local transit / entries: 1,500–3,000
- **Best night base:** **Arashiyama / Western Kyoto** if you want an even slower start the next morning; otherwise stay in **central Kyoto**

## Day 3 — Northern Temples and a Calm Garden Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/flower1.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Kinkaku-ji** very early, then continue to **Ryōan-ji** for a quieter, contemplative temple stop.
Media: Alt=Morning:** Visit **Kinkaku-ji** very early, then continue to **Ryōan-ji** for a quieter, contemplative temple stop, Kyoto, Japan
- **Afternoon:** Head to **Ninna-ji** or **Daitoku-ji** area for a less rushed temple circuit and more open walking space.
- **Food:** Have lunch near the temple area, then a low-key dinner back in central Kyoto.
Media: Alt=Food:** Have lunch near the temple area, then a low-key dinner back in central Kyoto, Kyoto, Japan
- **Estimated cost:** **JPY 18,000–25,000**
  - Lodging: 12,000–16,000
  - Food: 5,000–6,500
  - Local transit / entries: 1,000–2,500
- **Best night base:** **Central Kyoto / Karasuma** for easy access in all directions

## Day 4 — Day Trip to Uji
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Take a short train ride to **Uji** and visit **Byodo-in** early.
- **Afternoon:** Walk the river area, browse **matcha** shops, and keep the day relaxed with just 2–3 major stops.
- **Food:** Matcha dessert, tea soba, and a simple local lunch.
- **Estimated cost:** **JPY 16,000–22,000**
  - Lodging: 12,000–16,000
  - Food: 4,500–6,000
  - Transit / entries: 1,500–2,000
- **Best night base:** **Central Kyoto / Kawaramachi** for easy dining and return transit

## Day 5 — Fushimi and Departure Buffer
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Fushimi Inari Taisha** very early, then stop for a short sake-district walk if time allows.
- **Afternoon:** Keep the rest of the day open for shopping, a final meal, and departure logistics.
- **Food:** Try **inari sushi** or a final Kyoto-style lunch near Kyoto Station.
- **Estimated cost:** **JPY 15,000–21,000**
  - Lodging: 12,000–16,000
  - Food: 4,000–5,500
  - Transit / entries: 500–1,500
- **Best night base:** **Kyoto Station / Central Kyoto** if you have an evening departure

## Budget Fit for 2 Adults
- **Trip total estimate:** **JPY 86,000–118,000**
- This is comfortably within your stated budget of **USD 1,800**, leaving room for better meals, nicer lodging, or extra admissions.
- To keep crowd levels lower, prioritize **early starts**, **midday breaks**, and **fewer temple stops per day**.

# Neighborhoods That Work Best for Your Style

- **Gion / Higashiyama:** Best for temple access, evening walks, and classic Kyoto atmosphere
- **Karasuma / Central Kyoto:** Best all-around base with easy transit and dining
- **Kawaramachi / Downtown:** Best for food, shopping, and flexible evenings
- **Arashiyama:** Best if you want a scenic, slower night after exploring the west side
- **Kyoto Station area:** Best for arrival/departure convenience and simple logistics

# Spring Packing Checklist for Kyoto

- Light jacket or cardigan for cool mornings and evenings
- Comfortable walking shoes with good grip
- Compact umbrella or packable rain shell
- Layers: T-shirts, long-sleeve top, light sweater
- Socks you can wear with temple or indoor shoes
- Small day bag for water, wallet, and phone
- Portable charger
- Tissue pack and hand sanitizer
- Reusable water bottle
- Allergy medicine if you are sensitive to spring pollen
- Scarf or thin wrap for extra warmth on windy days

# Quick Actions
